<#
.SYNOPSIS
    SessionStart hook: one line saying which reviewers are out right now, and until when.

.DESCRIPTION
    Runs at the start of a Claude Code session in any project where the plugin is
    enabled (hooks/hooks.json). Prints ONE line to stdout, which Claude Code adds to the
    agent's context (wave 24, D14-D17 - the line `codex-providers.ps1 -Short` prints):

        codex-consult: out - openai :: gpt-6-astra (until Sun 20:35, in 2d 10h), gemini :: *
        (until Sun 21:30, in 2d 11h); 9 of 11 reviewers available

    or `codex-consult: all 11 reviewers available`. Every roster entry is judged with the
    roster walk's own verdict (Select-PanelMembers -All: credentials, the launch invariant,
    the endpoint health of THIS repository's ledgers - an auth failure, a usage limit with a
    reset ahead, one without a reset for 60 minutes after it was hit); the entries of one
    endpoint group that share the state collapse to `<label> :: *`; reset times are LOCAL
    with a rounded relative hint; nothing is cut. An entry whose check needs the network (the
    agy engine's `agy models`) is `not checked` here - "..., 2 not checked" in the count -
    unless THIS repository's ledgers hold a usable reply on that endpoint from the last 60
    minutes (then it is available); a recorded auth failure or usage limit still shows it
    out. The muse engine's sign-in check reads ~/.config/muse/auth.json locally and runs here
    too, as does its billing guard (`meta :: <model> (refused: META_API_KEY is set)`).
    Without a roster: the providers of the Codex config ("... (no reviewer roster)").

    When the Codex CLI is not on PATH: `codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow
    the setup-providers skill`. Everything else (an unreadable config, an unusable roster, a
    crash inside the check) is reported in the same one-line form and never fails the
    session: the exit code is always 0. No network call, no lock, nothing written: it runs
    `codex-providers.ps1 -Short -Json -NoNetwork` and prints the `line` of its object.

    Cost: about one second (`codex login status` for the built-in openai), once per
    session. Disable the hook by disabling the plugin's hooks in Claude Code settings.

    Runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    # Where consultations are stored (endpoint health is read from every task ledger
    # under it). Relative paths resolve against the git repo root of the current directory.
    [string]$CollabDir = '.collab'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$line = ''
try {
    $providers = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'codex-providers.ps1'
    $psExe = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
    $codex = Get-Command codex -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $codex) {
        $line = 'codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow the setup-providers skill before consulting a reviewer'
    } else {
        $previous = $ErrorActionPreference
        $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
        $raw = @(& $psExe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $providers -Short -Json -NoNetwork -CollabDir $CollabDir 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" })
        $code = $LASTEXITCODE
        $ErrorActionPreference = $previous
        $jsonStart = -1
        for ($i = 0; $i -lt $raw.Count; $i++) { if ($raw[$i] -match '^\s*\{') { $jsonStart = $i; break } }
        $obj = $null
        if ($jsonStart -ge 0) {
            try { $obj = (($raw[$jsonStart..($raw.Count - 1)]) -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { $obj = $null }
        }
        $text = $(if ($obj) { [string]$obj.line } else { '' })
        if ($text -match '^codex-consult: ' -and $text -notmatch "[`r`n]") {
            $line = $text
        } else {
            $first = (@($raw | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.Trim() }) | Select-Object -First 1)
            if (-not $first) { $first = "codex-providers.ps1 exited $code without output" }
            $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $first"
        }
    }
} catch {
    $msg = ("$($_.Exception.Message)" -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
    if ($msg.Length -gt 120) { $msg = $msg.Substring(0, 117) + '...' }
    $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $msg"
}
Write-Output $line
exit 0

# when, else the entry's `when`; a time in the future counts as now); HitIso; Until
# (RetryAfter, else Hit + 60 min) }. A usable reply is Test-UsableOutcome (a reply after a
# timeout continuation counts).
function Get-EndpointHealth {
    param([object[]]$Consults, [string]$Fingerprint, [datetime]$UtcNow = [datetime]::UtcNow)
    $h = [pscustomobject]@{ Auth = $null; Quota = $null; QuotaKnown = $false; LastLimit = $null; LastFailure = $null; RecentUsable = $null }
    if (-not $Fingerprint) { return $h }
    $nowOffset = New-Object DateTimeOffset ([datetime]::SpecifyKind($UtcNow, [DateTimeKind]::Utc))
    $records = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
    foreach ($c in @($Consults | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })) {
        $rev = Get-PropertyValue $c 'reviewer' $null
        $fp = if ($null -eq $rev) { $script:BuiltinOpenAiFingerprint } else { [string](Get-PropertyValue $rev 'provider_fingerprint' '') }
        if (-not $fp -or $fp -ne $Fingerprint) { continue }
        $outcome = [string](Get-PropertyValue $c 'bridge_outcome' '')
        if (-not $outcome) { continue }
        $at = ConvertTo-WhenOffset (Get-PropertyValue $c 'when' '')
        if ($null -eq $at) { continue }
        # A failure stamped in the future (clock skew, a mislabelled zone) counts as now:
        # its age is clamped to 0, it is never skipped (F15-4).
        $age = [Math]::Max(0, ($UtcNow - $at.UtcDateTime).TotalMinutes)
        # "Newest" is by COMPLETION (D9, F03-3): a panel's members start together and finish in
        # any order, so a member that started later may have succeeded before an earlier one hit
        # its usage limit. finished_at (0.4.x wave 21), else when + wall_seconds (older entries),
        # else when; ties by n (F02-5).
        $order = ConvertTo-WhenOffset (Get-PropertyValue $c 'finished_at' '')
        if ($null -eq $order) {
            $order = $at
            $ws = 0.0
            if ([double]::TryParse([string](Get-PropertyValue $c 'wall_seconds' ''), [System.Globalization.NumberStyles]::Float, $script:Invariant, [ref]$ws) -and $ws -gt 0) { $order = $at.AddSeconds($ws) }
        }
        $entryN = 0
        [void][int]::TryParse([string](Get-PropertyValue $c 'n' ''), [ref]$entryN)
        $rec = [pscustomobject]@{ At = $at; Order = $order; N = $entryN; Ok = (Test-UsableOutcome $outcome); Class = ''; Code = ''; Message = ''; When = $at.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:sszzz', $script:Invariant); AgeMinutes = [int][Math]::Max(0, [Math]::Floor($age)); Age = $age; RetryAfter = $null; RetryAfterIso = ''; RetryAfterBasis = ''; Hit = $at; HitIso = ''; Until = $at.AddMinutes(60) }
        if (-not $rec.Ok) {
            $reference = $at
            $pf = Get-PropertyValue $c 'provider_failure' $null
            if ($null -ne $pf) {
                $rec.Class = [string](Get-PropertyValue $pf 'class' 'unknown')
                # An entry recorded as auth whose message says usage limit / quota / rate limit
                # counts as quota (Get-ProviderFailureClass's rule, applied when the ledger is
                # READ): a 401/403 with a usage-limit text recorded before that rule existed
                # (Kimi Code's 5-hour limit) stops refusing the endpoint for 24 h as an auth
                # failure - without anyone editing the ledger.
                if ($rec.Class -eq 'auth' -and ([string](Get-PropertyValue $pf 'message' '')) -match $script:QuotaTextPattern) { $rec.Class = 'quota' }
                $rec.Code = [string](Get-PropertyValue $pf 'code' '')
                $rec.Message = [string](Get-PropertyValue $pf 'message' '')
                $pfWhen = ConvertTo-WhenOffset (Get-PropertyValue $pf 'when' '')
                if ($null -ne $pfWhen) { $reference = $pfWhen }
                $recorded = Get-PropertyValue $pf 'retry_after' $null
                if ($null -ne $recorded -and "$recorded") { $rec.RetryAfter = ConvertTo-WhenOffset $recorded }
            } else {
                # older entry: classify its bridge_outcome, lifting an SSE/JSON error payload
                $parsedOutcome = ConvertFrom-ProviderErrorText -Text $outcome
                $rec.Class = Get-ProviderFailureClass "$($parsedOutcome.Code) $outcome"
                $rec.Code = $parsedOutcome.Code
                $rec.Message = $parsedOutcome.Message
            }
            # an entry recorded without retry_after: read the reset time from its message now
            if ($null -ne $rec.RetryAfter) { $rec.RetryAfterBasis = 'ledger' }
            else {
                $rec.RetryAfter = Get-RetryAfter -Message $rec.Message -Reference $reference -ReferenceOffset
                if ($null -ne $rec.RetryAfter) { $rec.RetryAfterBasis = 'message (reference offset)' }
            }
            # (wave 24) when the failure happened - a time in the future counts as now (F15-4) -
            # and, without a reset time, the 60 minutes it stays out
            $hit = $reference
            if ($hit.UtcDateTime -gt $UtcNow) { $hit = $nowOffset.ToOffset($hit.Offset) }
            $rec.Hit = $hit
            $rec.HitIso = Format-OffsetIso $hit
            $rec.Until = $hit.AddMinutes(60)
            if ($null -ne $rec.RetryAfter) {
                $rec.RetryAfterIso = Format-OffsetIso $rec.RetryAfter
                $rec.Until = $rec.RetryAfter
            }
            if ($rec.Message.Length -gt 100) { $rec.Message = $rec.Message.Substring(0, 100) }
        }
        $records.Add($rec)
    }
    $sorted = @($records | Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { $_.Order }; Descending = $true }, @{ Expression = { $_.N }; Descending = $true })
    $auth = @($sorted | Where-Object { $_.Ok -or $_.Class -eq 'auth' }) | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($auth -and -not $auth.Ok -and $auth.AgeMinutes -le 24 * 60) { $h.Auth = $auth }
    $quota = @($sorted | Where-Object { $_.Ok -or $_.Class -eq 'quota' }) | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($quota -and -not $quota.Ok) {
        if ($null -ne $quota.RetryAfter) {
            if ($quota.RetryAfter.UtcDateTime -gt $UtcNow) { $h.Quota = $quota }
        } elseif ($quota.Until.UtcDateTime -gt $UtcNow) {
            $h.Quota = $quota
        }
    }
    $h.QuotaKnown = [bool]($h.Quota -and $null -ne $h.Quota.RetryAfter)
    $h.LastLimit = @($sorted | Where-Object { -not $_.Ok -and $_.Class -eq 'quota' -and $_.AgeMinutes -le 24 * 60 }) | Select-Object -First 1
    $h.LastFailure = @($sorted | Where-Object { -not $_.Ok -and $_.AgeMinutes -le 24 * 60 }) | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $h.LastLimit -and $h.Quota) { $h.LastLimit = $h.Quota }
    if (-not $h.LastFailure -and $h.Quota) { $h.LastFailure = $h.Quota }
    $h.RecentUsable = @($sorted | Where-Object { $_.Ok -and $_.Age -le 60 }) | Select-Object -First 1
    return $h
}

#
# The reviewer roster is an ordered list of reviewers the operator is willing to use, first

#   { "roster_version": 1,

#                    { "provider": "ZAI", "model": "glm-5.3" },
#                    { "provider": "local", "model": "m", "auth": "none",

#   model         optional: absent = the model resolves as without a roster (the Codex

# permission | capability | auth | quota | transport | unknown
function Get-ProviderFailureClass {
    param([string]$Message)
    foreach ($k in $script:FailureClassPatterns.Keys) {
        if ($k -eq 'auth' -and $Message -match $script:QuotaTextPattern) { return 'quota' }
        if ($Message -match $script:FailureClassPatterns[$k]) { return $k }
    }
    return 'unknown'
}

# The provider's own error inside a failure text: an SSE payload `data:{"error":{...}}`
# (MiMo sends its rejections that way) or a bare `{"error":{...}}` -> error.message and
# error.code; otherwise the text itself. { Code; Message }.
function ConvertFrom-ProviderErrorText {
    param([string]$Text)
    $r = [pscustomobject]@{ Code = ''; Message = (ConvertTo-OneLine $Text) }
    if (-not $Text) { return $r }
    $candidates = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    foreach ($m in [regex]::Matches($Text, '(?m)data:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$')) { $candidates.Add($m.Groups[1].Value) }
    $at = $Text.IndexOf('{"error"')
    if ($at -ge 0) { $candidates.Add($Text.Substring($at).Trim()) }
    foreach ($json in $candidates) {
        $o = $null
        try { $o = ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject $json } catch { continue }
        $e = Get-PropertyValue $o 'error' $null
        if ($null -eq $e) { continue }
        if ($e -is [string]) { $r.Message = ConvertTo-OneLine $e; return $r }
        $msg = [string](Get-PropertyValue $e 'message' '')
        if ($msg) { $r.Message = ConvertTo-OneLine $msg }
        $r.Code = [string](Get-PropertyValue $e 'code' '')
        if (-not $r.Code) { $r.Code = [string](Get-PropertyValue $e 'type' '') }
        return $r
    }
    return $r
}

# When a provider says its limit resets - read from its failure message, never guessed.
# Recognised (case-insensitive; a straight or a curly apostrophe makes no difference):
#   1. Codex's wording "try again at Sep 28th, 2026 8:35 PM." (also "resets at",
#      "available at", "until" before the same form; full or 3-letter month names; the
#      ordinal suffix, the comma, the year and AM/PM are optional - no AM/PM = a 24-hour
#      clock; no year = the reference's year, or the next one when that date lies more
#      than a day before the reference). Codex prints a WALL-CLOCK time of the machine it
#      runs on (ConvertFrom-WallClock).
#   2. an ISO-8601 timestamp after try again / retry / reset / until / available: with an
#      offset it is an instant; without one it is a wall-clock time like 1.
#   3. a duration: "retry after 30" / "Retry-After: 30s" (no unit = seconds), "retry after
#      1 week", "try again in 5 minutes", "resets in 2 days", "try again in 3 days 1 hour
#      7 minutes" (units w, d, h, m, s; the parts are summed) -> $Reference + it.
#   4. Google's wordings (the agy engine, 0.4.0): "retry in 32s", "retry in 1m5.3s" (Go
#      durations: h, m, s, ms, decimals), "retry in 90 seconds", and the gRPC RetryInfo
#      payload "retryDelay":{"seconds":32} / "retryDelay": "32s" / retryDelay: 32s ->
#      $Reference + it, fractions rounded UP to the next second.
#   5. a compact duration after resets / try again / retry / available in (0.4.x, the agy
#      quota "Individual quota reached. ... Resets in 68h58m18s."; also "in 2d3h", "in 45m",
#      "in 30s"; units w, d, h, m, s, ms, decimals) -> $Reference + it, rounded up.
#   6. a rolling window (0.4.x, Kimi Code: "You've reached your 5-hour usage limit. Your quota
#      will reset when the current 5-hour window ends.") -> $Reference + the window's length.
#      That is an UPPER BOUND, not the provider's own reset time: the window ends at the
#      latest one window length after the failure (it began at or before it). Tried last.
# Which offset (F15-1):
#   write time (New-ProviderFailure, on the machine that saw the failure): a wall-clock
#     time is read with the rules of -TimeZone (default [TimeZoneInfo]::Local), so a reset
#     on the far side of a daylight-saving change gets the offset valid THEN (Berlin: a
#     failure at 2026-10-25T01:00+02:00 saying "Oct 26th, 2026 8:35 PM" ->
#     2026-10-26T20:35:00+01:00). A time that does not exist (the spring gap) takes the
#     offset after the transition, an ambiguous one (the autumn overlap) the offset before
#     it. Instants are shown in that zone.
#   read time (-ReferenceOffset: a ledger entry recorded without retry_after): the reader's
#     zone may not be the recorder's, so the offset of $Reference (the failure's `when`) is
#     used for a wall-clock time and for display.
# DateTimeOffset, or $null when the message names no reset time.
$script:MonthNumbers = @{ 'jan' = 1; 'feb' = 2; 'mar' = 3; 'apr' = 4; 'may' = 5; 'jun' = 6; 'jul' = 7; 'aug' = 8; 'sep' = 9; 'oct' = 10; 'nov' = 11; 'dec' = 12 }
$script:DurationUnit = '(?:weeks?|wks?|w|days?|d|hours?|hrs?|h|minutes?|mins?|m|seconds?|secs?|s)\b'
$script:RetryAfterRe = @{
    Codex = [regex]('(?i)(?:try\s+again\s+(?:at|on|after)|resets?\s+(?:at|on)|available\s+(?:again\s+)?(?:at|on|after)|until)\s+' +
        '(?<mon>jan(?:uary)?|feb(?:ruary)?|mar(?:ch)?|apr(?:il)?|may|june?|july?|aug(?:ust)?|sep(?:t(?:ember)?)?|oct(?:ober)?|nov(?:ember)?|dec(?:ember)?)\.?\s+' +
        '(?<day>[0-9]{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\b,?\s*(?:(?<year>[0-9]{4})\b,?\s*)?(?:at\s+)?' +
        '(?<hour>[0-9]{1,2}):(?<min>[0-9]{2})(?::(?<sec>[0-9]{2}))?(?:\s*(?<ampm>[ap])\.?\s?m\b\.?)?')
    Iso   = [regex]'(?i)(?:try\s+again|retry|resets?|until|available)[^0-9\r\n]{0,24}?(?<date>[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})[T ](?<time>[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(?::[0-9]{2}(?:\.[0-9]+)?)?)(?<tz>Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})?'
    After = [regex]('(?i)retry[- ]after[:\s]\s*(?<n>[0-9]+)(?![0-9:.\-])(?:\s*(?<u>' + $script:DurationUnit + '))?')
    In    = [regex]('(?i)(?:try\s+again|resets?)\s+in\s+(?<parts>[0-9]+\s*' + $script:DurationUnit + '(?:(?:\s*,\s*|\s+and\s+|\s+)[0-9]+\s*' + $script:DurationUnit + ')*)')
    Part  = [regex]('(?i)(?<n>[0-9]+)\s*(?<u>' + $script:DurationUnit + ')')
    # Google: "retry in 32s" / "retry in 1m5.3s" (a Go duration) / "retry in 90 seconds"
    RetryIn = [regex]'(?i)\bretry\s+in\s+(?<dur>(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:ms|h|m|s))+(?![A-Za-z0-9])|[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?\s*(?:hours?|hrs?|minutes?|mins?|seconds?|secs?)\b(?:(?:\s*,\s*|\s+and\s+|\s+)[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?\s*(?:hours?|hrs?|minutes?|mins?|seconds?|secs?)\b)*)'
    # gRPC RetryInfo: "retryDelay":{"seconds":32} or "retryDelay": "32s" / retryDelay: 32s
    RetryDelay = [regex]'(?i)retryDelay"?\s*[:=]\s*(?:\{\s*"?seconds"?\s*:\s*"?(?<sec>[0-9]+)|"?(?<dur>(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:ms|h|m|s))+)(?![A-Za-z0-9]))'
    GoPart = [regex]'(?i)(?<n>[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*(?<u>ms|hours?|hrs?|h|minutes?|mins?|m|seconds?|secs?|s)'
    # a compact duration: "Resets in 68h58m18s", "in 2d3h", "in 45m", "in 30s"
    Compact = [regex]'(?i)\b(?:try\s+again|resets?|retry|available(?:\s+again)?)\s+in\s+(?<dur>(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:w|d|h|ms|m|s))+)(?![A-Za-z0-9])'
    CompactPart = [regex]'(?i)(?<n>[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)(?<u>w|d|h|ms|m|s)'
    # a rolling window: "reset when the current 5-hour window ends" (an UPPER BOUND)
    Window = [regex]'(?i)\bresets?\s+when\s+the\s+current\s+(?<n>[0-9]+)[- ](?<u>minute|hour|day|week)s?\s+window\s+ends'
}
# Seconds of a Go duration ("1m5.3s", "500ms") or a worded one ("90 seconds", "1 hour 30
# minutes"); decimals allowed; $null when nothing parses.
function ConvertFrom-GoDuration {
    param([string]$Text)
    $total = [double]0
    $any = $false
    foreach ($p in $script:RetryAfterRe.GoPart.Matches([string]$Text)) {
        $n = [double]::Parse($p.Groups['n'].Value, $script:Invariant)
        $u = $p.Groups['u'].Value.ToLowerInvariant()
        if ($u -eq 'ms') { $total += $n / 1000 }
        elseif ($u.StartsWith('h')) { $total += $n * 3600 }

So the explicit-run behavior is intentional and documented, but the wave's claim "out for exactly 60 minutes on every surface" is qualified how? Let's read the README/CHANGELOG wording for the 60-min rule to see whether the claim is overbroad (a doc defect) — that could be a legit finding (claim vs behaviour mismatch), especially since the brief's own claim 5 says "a usage limit without a reset time is out for exactly 60 minutes on every surface".

Let me check README/CHANGELOG statements.

item.text:
Very thorough tests. Now, where can I find a genuine new defect? Let me review areas the tests don't cover and the code looks fishy.

Candidate 1: In the timeout-continuation skip check (line 3014), the prefilter regex is narrower than the quota/auth class vocabulary (misses 'billing', '402', 'insufficient balance', 'payment required', 'token plan', 'credits? exhausted', 'credit balance', 'too many requests', 'plan exhausted'). Also misses 'permission'/'capability' (fine — those aren't skip reasons). The brief claims "no continuation after ... a quota/auth/billing failure". Billing is a quota-class word in the pattern table but not in the prefilter. So a killed muse turn whose stderr names "insufficient balance" (or 402 payment required / "billing") will not be caught → the bridge runs another turn against a provider that will bill/fail again. Evidence: read-code at codex-consult.ps1:3014 vs common.ps1:4300 quota pattern.

Hmm, but actually the prefilter's purpose is to select lines which are then classified. Missed lines = no skip. This is a genuine gap between the documented rule and the code. Severity: minor (the consequence is one wasted continuation turn that will fail anyway; the ledger records it). Given the brief explicitly says "no continuation after ... a quota/auth/billing failure", I'd call it minor→major. I'll say minor and note the practical impact (one extra paid turn on an empty balance; that's exactly what the rule exists to prevent — a billing failure can be a *real money* issue for a subscription/API key... actually for muse the launch guard would refuse before launch, since the billing guard is checked pre-launch; and for codex the failure would appear in stderr with 'error' text). Hmm — the '402'/'billing' words would be in the *provider's* message. Let me be careful: is it plausible that a killed turn's stderr contains "insufficient balance" but no other matched word (like "error")? The prefilter also matches `\berror\b`. DeepSeek's insufficient-balance message: "Error: Insufficient Balance" → matched by 'error' → classified quota. Hmm! Then the earlier word would be caught. So the gap narrows: the line must contain none of: error, usage limit, quota, rate limit, resource_exhausted, 429, unauthenticated, unauthorized, not signed in, 401, 403. "402 Payment Required" printed without the word "error"? e.g. a line "402 Payment Required: your credit balance is too low". '402' isn't in the prefilter (the class pattern has \b402\b but the prefilter doesn't) → missed. That's plausible for a raw HTTP status line. Still narrow. Severity: minor.

Candidate 2: `-ContinueSec` default = min(timeout,900) — but the panel PARENT computes ContinueSec and the members inherit. Fine.

Candidate 3: `$continueLastPath` cleanup: `if (-not $keepContinueLast -and $continueLastPath -and (Test-Path ...)) { Remove-Item }`. Let's check that the continuation's `-o` file is kept when needed (the commit-blocked path sets $keepContinueLast = $true). Looks handled.

Candidate 4: The salvage for the codex case reads `$eventsPath` — but for codex the main events path... fine.

Candidate 5: In the codex continuation, `$contRaw = (Read-SharedText -Path $continueLastPath).Trim()`. If the continuation process wrote the file but the file doesn't exist (e.g. -o not honored), Read-SharedText returns '' → `$continueProblem = 'empty reply'` → not continued. OK.

Candidate 6: `$wallSeconds` after the continuation: the summary/ledger `wall_seconds` is the main turn's wall (killed at T). The header line "Bridge outcome: ... Wall time: $wallSeconds s" — for a continued run, the header says "Wall time: 3600.4 s" and separately the continuation turn's wall. Could mislead but is documented.

Candidate 7: The panel member guard vs the continuation: the guard adds $ContinueSec but the member's CONTINUATION turn itself can be extended by... no repair on the continuation (the repair runs only if `$bridgeOutcome -eq 'usable reply'` after the continuation — wait! Interesting: after a successful continuation, `$repairEligible` requires `$bridgeOutcome -eq 'usable reply'` at line 3165, and the suffix is appended at 3390 (after). So after a successful continuation whose reply is prose, the format repair CAN run (resuming the thread again)! The guard accounts for TimeoutSec + min(TimeoutSec,300) repair + ContinueSec. Fine. But note: the repair turn is an extra turn beyond the documented "ONE more turn" — the doc says "Never more than one per consultation" referring to continuations, not repairs. The test (g) covers "a format repair killed on its timeout". Hmm, but does the doc/claim "no continuation after survivors" etc. mention that a repair can follow a continuation? Not needed.

Interesting: for the codex case in test (g), the repair turn resumes the thread; then the partial file's Turn 2 = "the format repair". OK.

Candidate 8: What about a continuation whose reply is prose and the repair is DISABLED (default? `-FormatRetry` default?). Probably 1. Fine.

Candidate 9 (availability): `Get-RosterAvailability` propagates an outage (auth/quota/quota-unknown-reset) across the group. But it does NOT propagate for the 'credentials' kind (missing env key) — correct, that's per-label. Fine.

Candidate 10: In codex-providers.ps1, the provider rows now use `Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk`. Consider a provider in the Codex config that is NOT in the roster at all and has a quota-unknown-reset: the row now reads unavailable (good). But consider the opposite: the built-in `openai` row when the roster exists but is not used... fine.

Hmm, here's a real one worth checking: `Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk` for a **single-run** row uses `$NoNetwork` — the row's verdict for the `-Short` no-roster case. Fine.

Candidate 11: The `-Short` line's count vs the hook. The hook prints `$obj.line`. `Format-AvailabilityLine` computes `$a of $n $noun available` and appends ", $o out, $c not checked" only when `$c -gt 0`. So when there are out entries and no not-checked, the count says "9 of 11 available" (implies 2 out, consistent). OK.

Now the F04-10 claim also said "the count has no rule for entries whose verdict is unknown" — now resolved.

Candidate 12: codex-providers `-Short` with `-Provider` refuses (Stop-WithError). Fine.

Candidate 13: the hook no longer reports which reviewer the roster would select — information regression vs the old line ("roster -> would select X"). README line 244 describes the new line as availability only; and the doc for the old behaviour is gone. But the hook's stated purpose in SKILL/setup-providers might still claim "would select"? Let's check setup-providers SKILL line 414: "expect `codex-consult: usable reply - <provider> :: <model>, …`" — that's from codex-consult output, different.

Hmm, that could be a doc drift: hooks/hooks.json description or README mention "roster -> would select". Let me grep the repo for "would select" to see whether the hook's documented output still promises it.

Line 2853/2891/2902/3355 are all before 3390, so they see the plain 'usable reply'. Good.

Wait — line 2902: that's inside the non-codex (agy) turn block, converting to "failed: $treeProblem" if the tree changed. And 3355 is a post-continuation tree check. Let me look at 3340-3365 to see the tree check after the continuation: if the CONTINUATION changed the tree, the outcome becomes failed. OK.

Now — a subtle but potentially important issue: the tree check for the continuation. After a successful continuation, `$bridgeOutcome = 'usable reply'` but then the post-continuation tree check (line 3355) may set "failed: $treeProblem". If the tree changed, then the reply is discarded (bridge_outcome failed) yet... would the salvage run? `$partialNeeded = ($mainTimedOut -and -not $continued) -or ...` — $continued is TRUE, so partialNeeded = false (unless retryKilled/repairKilled). So a usable continuation reply discarded by the tree check leaves NO partial and bridge_outcome failed — the reply file is still kept (replyPath written?). Hmm, that's the pre-existing behaviour for the main turn too (an agy tree-change turns a usable reply into failed, and the reply file is kept as the handoff?). Fine, pre-existing pattern.

Let me now check one more important thing about the continuation: the codex `-ContinueSec` continuation is launched via Invoke-EngineTurn which sets `$pendingRecord.state = 'launching'` and the events path = continueEventsPath, and `$extraEvents.Add("handoffs/$continueEventsName")`. Does the record name the continuation's event stream so a kill during the continuation can be recovered/resumed? Let's check what happens if the bridge itself is killed during the continuation: the record has `events` = the continuation's stream (Invoke-EngineTurn sets it before start). Then the next run consumes it and may salvage? The D3 recovery path reads the record's events. Plausibly handled (the salvage uses `$eventsPath` when there's no continuation turn...). Edge case, skip.

Now let's examine the `-Range` + panel member prompt: the member gets range_stat from the spec ✓.

Now check the DEFAULTS claim vs the SKILL/README: "acceptance 3600". The timeouts were raised; the plugin's default `-TimeoutSec` param value? Let's check the param default (line ~345). If the param has a default value of 900 and the code checks `$PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('TimeoutSec')`, then callers (like the hook, or other scripts calling codex-consult.ps1 with -TimeoutSec) are unaffected. But what about `codex-consult.ps1` being invoked by other plugins/tools with an explicit `-TimeoutSec 900`? Fine.

Hmm, what about the `panelSpec` path: `$memberTimeoutSource` ✓.

Now a genuinely risky one: **`$TimeoutSec` purpose default when Purpose is ''** → 900 (unchanged). ✓

Another: the timeout increase means a single consultation can now run 3600 s (1 h) with the lock held. The task lock (`-Panel`) and per-task serialization... not our concern.

Now the last area: F02-11's group availability. Get-RosterAvailability merges groups by fingerprint across ALL entries. For agy entries: "every agy label - they share one Google sign-in" — Get-EndpointGroups merges labels sharing a fingerprint. Do all agy entries share one fingerprint? The fingerprint comes from Resolve-ReviewerIdentity for the engine: let's check Resolve-EngineIdentity — it probably builds a fingerprint with the launcher. If each agy label produces a different fingerprint (e.g. including the model or label), they would NOT merge, so an outage on one agy entry would not mark the other agy entries out — contradicting the doc's parenthetical "every agy label - they share one Google sign-in". Let me check Resolve-EngineIdentity and Get-EntryFingerprint for engines.

Key: `$id.Fingerprint = Get-Sha256Hex(CompatString)` where CompatString = "cc-engine-v1|<name>" (per engine, not per launcher or label!). Let me verify: `$spec.CompatString` — the spec's CompatString is 'cc-engine-v1|<engine name>'. Let's check the engine table (line ~3050-3140) to confirm CompatString/HostName per engine.

Confirmed: fingerprint per engine (CompatString 'cc-engine-v1|agy'), so ALL agy roster labels share one fingerprint → the endpoint group merges all agy entries. Matches the doc. Also all agy entries share one endpoint, and Get-PanelPlan serializes them. Good.

Hmm, wait. That means for the codex-providers rows: engine rows are one row per LABEL, each with the engine's fingerprint → the same health for all agy labels. Fine.

But now here's a thought about a *new* issue: since all agy labels share one fingerprint, Get-RosterAvailability's group merge will collapse ALL agy entries into one group — so the -Short line prints "gemini :: *" only when all entries of the group share state and short phrase. Fine.

Now, a real question for the availability claim: `Get-RosterAvailability` propagates an outage across a group when the group member's Kind is auth/quota/quota-unknown-reset. For the agy group, an outage found by querying the endpoint health of the agy fingerprint applies to all → each already reports it individually anyway. Fine.

Let me now check something different and higher-yield: the `codex-providers.ps1` engine rows loop builds `$rosterPositions` from entries of that label, and `roster_selected` compares label+engine — with two codex providers of the same label? n/a.

But F02-10's claim was: "codex-providers emits one row per provider label and records only the first roster position/model; multi-model labels collapse or disappear" and the trigger: "two models on one label with one unavailable". For the TABLE (not -Short), the row's verdict is computed from the FIRST entry's model via `Resolve-ReviewerIdentity -Provider $el.Name -Model $model` where `$model` = the first entry's model. So if a label `gemini` has two models (pro and flash) and only `gemini :: flash` is out... the verdict is per-endpoint (fingerprint = engine), so both are out anyway. For a codex label with two models on ONE base_url (same endpoint): health is per endpoint → same verdict. So per-label rows are consistent for verdicts. The remaining F02-10 concern was the *hook*, now fixed via -Short -Json per entry. So: F02-10 = fixed (with a note that the table rows remain per label by design, and the -Short/-Json per-entry view is what the hook reads).

Hmm, but wait: is that entirely true? Consider a codex provider label `byteplus` with entries `byteplus :: kimi-k2.5` and `byteplus :: dola-seed-2.0-pro` — same label, same base_url → same fingerprint → same health. So both rows collapse. OK.

But what about the *credential* per entry? Same label → same table → same credential. OK, so per-label rows are a faithful projection for codex. For an engine label with several models, credentials/health are engine-wide. So F02-10 truly is only about the hook/line, which is now per-entry. Good.

Now, let's hunt in an area with no tests: `-Range` in a panel where the member is launched by a *different* repository root? The member runs in `-WorkingDirectory $callerCwd`; Get-RangeStat uses `$repoRoot`. Fine.

Next: check the README/-Short/-Short -Json exit code: `-Short` exits 0 always, even when a roster is unusable? If the roster is unusable, Stop-WithError → exit 1, no JSON. The hook handles that (falls back to the failure line). Documented ("unusable roster ... reported in the same one-line form"). ✓ (test HOOK asserts that).

Now let me check the CHANGELOG to see the claims, and compare with README's mention of "-ContinueSec" default for panel members etc. Also confirm that the docs mention what happens when the continuation succeeds: `bridge_outcome` counts as usable "everywhere". We verified scoreboard/findings/exit code.

Let me check `codex-findings.ps1 -Rate` and any place that decides "the reviewer failed, rate it" using `-like 'failed*'`: line 291 `if ($outcome -like 'failed*') { $verdict = 'failed' }` — a continued reply gets verdict from the parse; fine.

What about `Test-PendingActive`/recovery code paths that check `first_reply` or the pending record's outcome for a continued run? Let's grep 'first_reply'.
